tonight.headline: Still 40.8 to nothing, and the only thing that changed tonight is that your one open card broke.
body: The scoreboard is untouched since this afternoon: Josh Allen's 40.8 against Detroit is the only score in this matchup and Panda Attack have not put a player on the field. ESPN still reads 59%, which is honest rather than pessimistic — they have nine unplayed starters to your eight, and both rosters run out to Monday night.

There is nothing to do about the matchup tonight. There is something to do about the roster: the Rashod Bateman card this brief published six hours ago does not survive the reporting, and the replacement is below.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Panda Attack start Saquon Barkley, Chase Brown and Javonte Williams at running back with Dak Prescott at quarterback. Prescott is at home against Washington in the 50.5-point game that is the highest total on the Week 2 board, with Dallas implied 27.0. If that game goes the way the market prices it, a 34.7-point deficit closes inside one afternoon.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing you can act on. Your lineup is locked in the sense that matters — every start is correct on today's reporting and no bench player projects above the man in front of him. The matchup resolves Monday when Likely and their Rams pieces play.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Both games kick 11:00 Sunday Mexico City
doFirst.title: Drop Kyle Pitts, add Mark Andrews
doFirst.subtitle: Fifth run carrying the Pitts half and the fourth name proposed for the other half. This is the first one that survived a search.

case.label: Why the name changed again, tonight
case.body: This afternoon's brief said Rashod Bateman. DraftKings Network published his Week 1 usage after that went out: a 4.2% target share, last among ten Baltimore receivers, one target, zero catches, zero air yards. Chris Moore, LaJohntay Wester and Ja'Kobi Lane all out-targeted him. A receiver who is tenth in his own huddle does not become the beneficiary of an absence just because the absence is large. The card was wrong and it is being killed the same day rather than next week.

case.label: Who actually inherits the targets
case.body: The same piece puts Andrews first in line: he and Zay Flowers each commanded 25% of Baltimore's targets in Week 1. Flowers is DOUBTFUL with a hamstring on the final report. Baltimore carry a 27.75 implied total, the highest of any team any AVIATO player is on, against a New Orleans defence implied at 19.25 that allowed 206 receiving yards, two scores and seven red-zone targets in Week 1.

case.label: Why this is not the Andrews card I declined four times
case.body: The standing decline says adding Andrews creates a second tight end who cannot enter Chem's RB/WR flex — a dead seat. That objection is about adding him. It does not apply when the outgoing player is the dead seat: Pitts already occupies it. This swaps the occupant of a seat that exists either way, at a projection of 10.4 against 10.4, so STRATEGY's floor on lowering projected points is not touched. Pitts's is also the only seat on this roster outside the seven-day churn window — Coker, Loop and the Ravens defence all arrived on 16 September.

case.label: The drop, unsoftened
case.body: Atlanta confirmed Cooper Rush as the Week 2 starter today with Michael Penix Jr. ruled out and Tua Tagovailoa out. Pitts is a tight end who cannot start in this league behind a third-string quarterback on a team implied for 21.5. He is 93.4% rostered, which makes him the only genuine trade chip on the roster, and that is the one real cost of this move — stated rather than hidden. No Chem team has lost its starting tight end, so the chip has no buyer this week.

case.label: Two sources disagree and I am picking a side
case.body: Sports Illustrated ran both 'Andrews should be started with Zay Flowers injured' and a must-sit list with Andrews on it. The must-sit piece describes Baltimore facing Cleveland and calls Isaiah Likely inactive — Likely has been a Giant all season and Baltimore play New Orleans. It is a dated article and I discarded it. The must-start read is the one I am taking.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Zay Flowers is ACTIVE on Sunday's inactive list, which restores Andrews to third in Baltimore behind Flowers and Bateman and makes this a hold. Or Isaiah Likely appears on the Giants' Saturday report, which makes Pitts the only tight end on the roster and kills the outgoing half. Or Andrews finishes outside the top twelve tight ends in Week 2 while Pitts clears five targets — then the seat was never the problem and the churn cost a chip for nothing.

action.label: Add Mark Andrews · drop Kyle Pitts

whatWentWrong.title: The Bateman card lasted six hours
whatWentWrong.lead: This brief published 'drop Pitts, add Bateman' at 22:10 UTC. The usage data that kills it was already public. A 4.2% target share, last of ten Baltimore receivers.

case.label: What was missed
case.body: The card was built from Baltimore's own Friday notes naming Bateman as the man who steps up if Flowers sits — a team-site quote about the depth chart, not about the ball. Nobody paired it with what Bateman did with his Week 1 snaps: one target, no catches, no air yards, behind Chris Moore and LaJohntay Wester. The runbook's own test is whether a card contains something a column sort could not produce. It did. It was just the wrong something.

case.label: What it cost
case.body: Nothing yet, because it was never fired — the card went out six hours before this correction and Atlanta do not kick until Sunday. That is the second time in three days this seat has been saved by the owner not acting quickly on a card telling him to act quickly, which is not a system working.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If Bateman draws eight or more targets at New Orleans on Sunday, the read was wrong and the Week 1 share was the anomaly rather than the signal. Logged, and it will be reported either way.

whatWentWrong.title: Four names in five runs for one bench seat
whatWentWrong.lead: Mack Hollins three times, Rashod Bateman once, now Mark Andrews. The outgoing half has been right since 16 September and the incoming half has been researched properly only tonight.

case.label: The pattern
case.body: Each name came from a column naming a beneficiary — FantasyPros on Hollins, Baltimore's own site on Bateman — and none was checked against what the player actually did with the ball in Week 1. Hollins had 4 targets; Bateman had 1. Andrews had 25% of the team's targets. That check takes one search and it has now been skipped twice.

case.label: Why it connects to the card above
case.body: It is the reason the card above leads with usage rather than with a depth chart, and the reason its falsification clause is written against Andrews's target count rather than against Flowers's designation. If this one is wrong too, the seat stays shut until Week 2 results are in.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A fifth wrong name. If Andrews does not clear six targets with Flowers out, the correct answer for this seat was to hold Pitts all along, and the next run should stop proposing replacements for it until there is a genuine difference-maker on the wire.

Four more carry grades researched yesterday rather than tonight, and each says so in its own tile.

Yesterday's run verified he was full on Friday and off the report; I did not re-retrieve that, so I am reporting the history rather than overwriting their check.

worthALook.name: Khalil Shakir
worthALook.lead: Unchanged, and unchanged is still correct — he clears on 23 September, after his own Week 2 game, so nothing about him is actionable before his line is public.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: 69% rostered nationally and sitting on waivers here in a ten-team league. That is the ownership band STRATEGY section 4 calls the strongest single wire signal, because it usually means a manager blundered rather than that the player is bad.

case.label: Why waiting costs nothing
case.body: His clearsAt is 07:00 UTC on 23 September — Tuesday night in Mexico City, after Buffalo have played. Chem's waiver priority resets weekly and AVIATO sit 10th of 10, so there is no priority to protect and no early-bird advantage to capture.

case.label: No new Buffalo reporting
case.body: Third consecutive run with nothing retrievable on his role. The six-target test against Detroit is the whole of the case and it resolves Sunday.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Six or more targets against Detroit makes him a free claim on Wednesday 23 September, with the drop being whoever of Monangai or Brian Thomas Jr. had the worse Sunday. Fewer than six and this row closes.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: The largest season projection of any receiver on this wire at 182.4, free at 77% rostered, and still not an add tonight for two reasons that have not changed.

case.label: Confirmed tonight
case.body: CBS report him limited at Friday's practice with the thumb but carrying no injury designation for Denver. He played through the same thumb in Week 1. A thumb on a receiver is a catch-rate injury and his ownership is falling 0.41 a day, which is the market selling the injury rather than buying the role.

case.label: The concentration problem
case.body: AVIATO already hold Bhayshul Tuten and Brian Thomas Jr. from Jacksonville. STRATEGY section 8 names a Week 7 Jaguars problem in this league by name — Tuten, the Jaguars D/ST and Cam Little are all out together. A third Jaguar deepens a hole already on the calendar.

case.label: A live disagreement in the sourcing
case.body: One CBS item puts Meyers at two targets in the Week 1 blowout; another CBS headline says seven targets tied for the team lead. I could not reconcile them and I am not building on either. The Sunday count settles it.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Meyers out-targets Brian Thomas Jr. at Denver on Sunday, the swap is Meyers in for Thomas on Tuesday 22 September — Thomas's own thesis is the one that breaks, so the Jacksonville count does not rise. If Thomas wins the target battle, this row closes.

doNotChase.name: Rashod Bateman
doNotChase.lead: This brief told you to add him six hours ago. It was wrong, and the reversal is published here rather than quietly deleted.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: A 4.2% target share in Week 1 — last among ten Baltimore receivers. One target, zero catches, zero air yards. Chris Moore, LaJohntay Wester and Ja'Kobi Lane all out-targeted him. Baltimore threw 25 times and ran 37 while Derrick Henry went for 163 and three scores.

case.label: Why the ownership is spiking anyway
case.body: He is rising 2.93 a day, the fastest mover on this wire, which is the market buying the Flowers absence and attaching the most expensive name to it. That is the 'hot name on low volume' pattern STRATEGY section 4 calls a sell signal rather than a buy.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Eight or more targets at New Orleans on Sunday. That would make the Week 1 share the anomaly and put him back on the list at a much higher price.

doNotChase.name: Rachaad White
doNotChase.lead: The top why=OWNED running back on this wire at 66% rostered, researched tonight for the first time, and he is a committee back in the worst shape for this format.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 27 offensive snaps in his Commanders debut against Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 33. Seven carries for 22 yards, two catches on three targets for five. Croskey-Merritt leads the ground game; White is the passing-down back on a split.

case.label: Why full PPR does not rescue him
case.body: Three targets is not a receiving role. STRATEGY section 2 says a committee back who loses the goal line is uniquely bad in this format because he collects the least valuable touches available, and five receiving yards is what that looks like.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Croskey-Merritt missing a game, or White clearing five targets in a week. Either turns a committee body into a role.

doNotChase.name: Xavier Worthy
doNotChase.lead: 74% rostered nationally and free here, which is the ownership anomaly this roster is supposed to hunt. The reporting says take the miss.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Patrick Mahomes averaged 1.1 air yards per completion in Week 1, the lowest in the league, and went 0-for-4 on throws ten or more yards downfield. Worthy took 76.9% of his snaps out wide and caught three of six. Sharp Football Analysis grade him a WR4/FLEX.

case.label: Why the anomaly is real and still not enough
case.body: STRATEGY section 4 ranks ownership anomaly third, behind opportunity and a vacated role. Worthy has neither: nobody is hurt in front of him and the offence is throwing short by design. A deep threat on a checkdown offence is a structural mismatch, not a bargain.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Kansas City's air-yards profile normalising over two weeks, or Rashee Rice missing time. Rice is off the injury report entirely this week, so that second branch is closed for now.

settled.result: Wrong and fully resolved. Atlanta named Cooper Rush the Week 2 starter with Penix ruled out and Tua out. The call on Pitts never depended on it.

settled.result: The claim itself was right — Coker went 8 for 138 and two scores. Calling it settled as a miss because the drop was mispriced: Stafford is QB11 and was free in this league within two days.

settled.title: Hold Isaiah Likely over Kyle Pitts at tight end (14 September)
settled.result: Held again tonight. Likely is absent from the Giants' Week 2 report; Pitts is behind a third-string quarterback and is tonight's drop.

settled.title: Start Terry McLaurin in the RB/WR flex over Coker and Tuten (15 September)
settled.result: Held. McLaurin is absent from Washington's final Week 2 report in the highest-total game on the board. Coker is the live challenger and the gap narrowed: he led Carolina on a 26.5% target share. Held on game environment and route share, not comfortably.

settled.title: Hold Justin Jefferson through the Minnesota quarterback change (17 September)
settled.result: Held. Kyler Murray is officially out with a concussion and Carson Wentz starts. You do not bench WR5 on a quarterback.

settled.title: Decline Jordan Addison for the wire (16 September, six runs)
settled.result: Held. No new Minnesota reporting retrieved tonight and no trigger fired.

settled.title: Hold Brian Thomas Jr. through the shoulder scare (12 September, reviewed seven times)
settled.result: Held. No injury designation for Week 2 despite a limited week. The production half is still unproven at 3 catches for 40.

settled.title: Hold Kyle Monangai rather than drop him for a wire back (16 September)
settled.result: Held. Chicago carry the best implied total on the roster at 27.5 and nothing on the wire out-researches him.

settled.title: Hold Tyler Loop at kicker (16 September, six consecutive runs)
settled.result: Held. K4 at Pro Football Network and Baltimore implied 27.75, the highest total on your roster.

settled.title: Hold the Ravens defence rather than churn to San Francisco (16 September)
settled.result: Held, and vindicated on the board rather than on faith: FantasyPros rank Baltimore 3rd this week and San Francisco 4th. The churn would have cost a move to move backwards.

settled.title: Find no Chem trade worth proposing (17 September)
settled.result: Held. The Guillo-tinas surplus — Lamar Jackson starting with Patrick Mahomes benched in a one-QB league — is still the most interesting shape in the league and still does not help a roster that starts Josh Allen. George Kittle carries no designation this week, so the Pitts-as-chip trigger has not fired.

cannotSee.label: This run fired at 22:14 Friday Mexico City, not 16:00
cannotSee.body: The schedule describes this as the 4:00 PM refresh and says a morning run already published today. Neither is true of this firing: the previous brief went out at 22:10 UTC on 18 September, which was 16:05 Friday local, and this one is six hours behind it at 22:14 Friday local. Nothing in the analysis depends on the label, but the deadline arithmetic in this brief is computed from 04:14 UTC on 19 September and you should read it that way.

cannotSee.label: Whether Zay Flowers actually plays, which is the whole Andrews card
cannotSee.body: He is DOUBTFUL with a hamstring on Baltimore's final report and the club call him day-to-day. Doubtful is roughly a 25% play rate historically. The inactive list does not publish until ninety minutes before kickoff, long after this brief is written, and if he plays the Andrews add is a hold rather than a mistake.

cannotSee.label: Two tiles are dashed and four are borrowed from yesterday
cannotSee.body: Dashed: Kyle Pitts and Kyle Monangai — I retrieved nothing on Carolina's or Minnesota's defences this run. Borrowed rather than re-researched: Terry McLaurin, Bhayshul Tuten, Brian Thomas Jr. and the Dallas single-high figure, all carried from the 18 September run and marked as such in their tiles. Week 1 defensive metrics do not go stale in six hours, but they are not this run's work and you should not read them as a second confirmation.

cannotSee.label: Positional defence ranks barely exist in Week 2
cannotSee.body: Every grade above is built on one game of 2026 data plus last season's shape and this week's betting market. The runbook says defence grades before Week 4 are judgement rather than data, and that is exactly what these are. The implied totals are the hardest number in any tile on this page.

cannotSee.label: A dated Sports Illustrated article nearly went into the Andrews card
cannotSee.body: Their Week 2 must-sit tight ends piece lists Andrews, describes Baltimore facing Cleveland and calls Isaiah Likely inactive. Likely has been a Giant all season and Baltimore play New Orleans. It is last season's article on a current-looking URL. Discarded, and recorded because it is the second dated source this log has caught in a week.

cannotSee.label: Rivals' pending waiver claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN only ever returns AVIATO's own. If another Chem manager has a claim in on Andrews it will not appear anywhere in this brief — though he is a free agent here, so the add is instant and uncontested if you make it before someone else does.

cannotSee.label: Season projections are still frozen
cannotSee.body: seasonProj has returned identical figures across every snapshot this week. Until that is disproven it is a preseason artifact, which is why there is no trade in this brief priced on it and why the Pitts chip is described by ownership rather than by season value.

cannotSee.label: This brief does not refresh
cannotSee.body: It is as old as the chat that wrote it. Saturday's Atlanta, Carolina and Giants reports all land after this brief is finished, and the Giants file one more than anyone else because they play Monday.
